function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Java** is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language that was originally developed by James Gosling and his team at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle Corporation). It was first released in 1995 as part of the Sun Microsystems Java platform.

---

## 1. Core Characteristics

| Feature | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Platform‑independent** | Java code is compiled into *bytecode* that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The same bytecode works on any operating system that has a compatible JVM. |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything is an object (except primitives). Inheritance, encapsulation, polymorphism, and abstraction are first‑class concepts. |
| **Strongly typed** | Variables must be declared with a type, and type checking happens at compile time. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Garbage collection automatically frees memory that is no longer referenced. |
| **Rich standard library** | The Java Standard Edition (SE) includes APIs for collections, networking, I/O, concurrency, GUI (Swing/JavaFX), and more. |
| **Security** | The JVM sandbox, bytecode verification, and security manager help protect against malicious code. |
| **Multithreading** | Built‑in support for concurrent execution via the `java.lang.Thread` class and higher‑level concurrency utilities (`java.util.concurrent`). |

---

## 2. Typical Use Cases

| Domain | Why Java is a good fit |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Enterprise applications** | Mature frameworks (Spring, Jakarta EE) and robust ecosystem. |
| **Android apps** | Android’s runtime (ART) is based on the Dalvik/ART VM, which is a derivative of the JVM. |
| **Web servers & microservices** | High performance, scalability, and a vast array of libraries (e.g., Netty, Vert.x). |
| **Big data & analytics** | Hadoop, Spark, Flink, and other big‑data tools are written in Java or provide Java APIs. |
| **Embedded systems** | Java ME (Micro Edition) and Java SE Embedded target resource‑constrained devices. |
| **Desktop applications** | Swing, JavaFX, and third‑party UI toolkits. |

---

## 3. How Java Works (The Compile‑Run Cycle)

1. **Source code** (`.java`) →  
2. **Compiler** (`javac`) → **Bytecode** (`.class`) →  
3. **JVM** interprets or just‑in‑time compiles the bytecode → **Native machine code** → **Execution**.

Because the JVM abstracts the underlying hardware, the same `.class` files run on Windows, macOS, Linux, and many other platforms.

---

## 4. Common Java Syntax

```java
// A simple “Hello, World!” program
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, World!");
    }
}
```

* `public class HelloWorld` – declares a public class named `HelloWorld`.  
* `public static void main(String[] args)` – the entry point for a Java application.  
* `System.out.println(...)` – prints text to the console.

---

## 5. Java vs. JavaScript (Common Confusion)

| Aspect | Java | JavaScript |
|--------|------|------------|
| **Origin** | 1995, Sun Microsystems | 1995, Netscape |
| **Primary use** | Server‑side, desktop, Android, embedded | Client‑side web scripting, Node.js |
| **Execution** | JVM (bytecode) | Browser engine or V8 (Node.js) |
| **Typing** | Static, strong | Dynamic, weak |
| **Paradigm** | Object‑oriented, procedural | Prototype‑based, functional |

Despite the similar names, they are unrelated languages.

---

## 6. Popular Java Ecosystem

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Build tools** | Maven, Gradle, Ant |
| **Testing** | JUnit, TestNG, Mockito |
| **Dependency injection** | Spring Framework, CDI (Jakarta EE) |
| **Web frameworks** | Spring MVC, Jakarta EE (formerly Java EE), Micronaut |
| **ORM** | Hibernate, MyBatis |
| **Reactive** | Reactor, RxJava, Akka |
| **IDE** | IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans |

---

## 7. Quick Start (Using the Command Line)

1. **Install JDK** (Java Development Kit).  
   ```bash
   # On Ubuntu
   sudo apt install openjdk-21-jdk
   ```
2. **Create a file** `Hello.java` with the code above.  
3. **Compile**  
   ```bash
   javac Hello.java
   ```
4. **Run**  
   ```bash
   java Hello
   ```

You should see `Hello, World!` printed.

---

## 8. Where to Learn More

| Resource | Type | Link |
|----------|------|------|
| Official Java Tutorials | Interactive | https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/ |
| Java SE Documentation | Reference | https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/ |
| “Effective Java” (Joshua Bloch) | Book | https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/effective-java-3rd/9780134686097/ |
| “Java Concurrency in Practice” | Book | https://jcip.net/ |
| Online courses (Coursera, Udemy, Pluralsight) | Video | Search “Java programming” |

---

### TL;DR

Java is a versatile, platform‑independent, object‑oriented language that powers everything from enterprise back‑ends and Android apps to big‑data frameworks and embedded devices. Its strong typing, rich libraries, and mature ecosystem make it a go‑to choice for many developers worldwide.
